sentences.text: Callawayasaurus was a large plesiosaur, a marine reptile, belonging to the family Elasmosauridae. It reached a total body length between 7.4 and 8 meters, with a skull measuring 35 cm.

Its elongated nares, or nostrils, were positioned over the maxilla, which contained between 3 and 5 teeth. The neck contained 56 vertebrae, which were relatively short compared to other elasmosaurids.
Fossils of this animal lack pectoral bars, a structural element found in other plesiosaur species.
The neck of Callawayasaurus contained 56 vertebrae, which were relatively short compared to other elasmosaurids.
A nearly complete skeleton found to be more robust than the holotype suggests that Callawayasaurus may have exhibited sexual dimorphism.

The species was originally described by Samuel Paul Welles in 1962 as Alzadasaurus colombiensis and later reclassified into the genus Callawayasaurus by Kenneth Carpenter in 1999. The genus name honors the paleontologist Jack M. Callaway. The first remains were discovered in the Paja Formation near Leiva, Boyaca, Colombia.
Callawayasaurus lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 112 million years ago.
